play_next_surface_label: Example autoplay, end-screen, and play-next posture for official voter-information media routes
delivery_role_note: The service reviews official recordings and attached play-next surfaces so autoplay, end screens, cards, and other next-step pivots remain subordinate to the current recording and the named help lane rather than quietly becoming an invisible authority lift into another route.

reviewed_play_next_contexts.context_note: Reviewed whether the player could continue automatically to another video after playback and whether that continuation stayed inside a reviewed official scope.
Reviewed end screens or cards the office configured to point to other official recordings, playlists, channels, or follow-up routes.
Reviewed player-managed more-videos, related-video, or next-step surfaces that could feel like seamless continuity rather than a new answer surface.
Reviewed cards, CTA buttons, or end screens that could hand the viewer to another site or service from inside the player.

play_next_provenance_note: The service distinguishes office-curated next destinations from platform-shaped autoplay, more-videos, or recommendation surfaces.
autoplay_boundary_note: A video that starts automatically after the current recording ends is treated as a new public-answer surface unless the office explicitly reviews and stands behind that continuation as the intended next official route.
embed_and_player_handoff_note: Embedded-player autoplay, end screens, and in-player pivots are reviewed as handoff surfaces rather than silent continuity because the voter may stay inside the same page frame while the authority context changes.
external_pivot_boundary_note: Cards, CTA buttons, or end screens that can leave the current route are not treated as seamless continuity; they preserve recovery to the current written help lane and make the handoff legible.
current_help_recovery_note: When autoplay, cards, or after-video surfaces could mislead, the route points back to the current official page, reviewed FAQ/help entry, or named office contact instead of pretending the next media item is automatically controlling.
